decisive_items: Gram stain showed thin, fusiform gram-negative rods in two of four bottles
sustained a dog bite on her right thumb approximately one week before admission
response.rationale: Dog bite plus fusiform gram-negative rods in blood cultures strongly indicate Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis; thrombocytopenia and rash are secondary to sepsis. TTP lacks schistocytes and DIC lacks coagulopathy evidence.

rejected.why: GI bleeding not supported by normal haptoglobin/fibrinogen and no melena/hematemesis; low iron/macrocytosis nonspecific.
No schistocytes on smear and normal haptoglobin/fibrinogen argue against TTP; petechiae and thrombocytopenia better explained by sepsis.
DIC requires coagulopathy (elevated PT/PTT, low fibrinogen) which are normal; no schistocytes or bleeding.
